top1Income.definition: share of the top 1% of pre-tax national income, equal-split adults (20+): WID sptincj992 p99p100 (sptinc992j / shweal992j)
top1Income.source: World Inequality Database (WID.world), bulk download version 2026-10-15, WID_data_RU.csv; data-quality grade 3 of 5 (WID counts income grades 3+ and wealth grades 1+ as observed, https://wid.world/data-quality/)
top1Income.note: Russia's territory, not the whole USSR: WID's USSR file holds no share series. Novokmet, Piketty & Zucman (2018), 'From Soviets to oligarchs', updated by Neef (2022).

stateFirms.definition: the state's share of the means of production by law: the basic means of production in industry, construction and agriculture, transport and communication, and the banks are state property
stateFirms.source: Constitution (Fundamental Law) of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, adopted at the Seventh (Special) Session of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR, Ninth Convocation, on October 7, 1977 (Novosti Press Agency translation)
stateFirms.quote: Article 10. The foundation of the economic system of the USSR is socialist ownership of the means of production in the form of state property (belonging to all the people), and collective farm-and-co-operative property. Socialist ownership also embraces the property of trade unions and other public organisations which they require to carry out their purposes under these rules. The state protects socialist property and provides conditions for its growth. No one has the right to use socialist property for person gain or other selfish ends. || Article 11. State property, i. e. the common property of the Soviet people, is the principal form of socialist property. The land, its minerals, waters, and forests are the exclusive property of the state. The state owns the basic means of production in industry, construction, and agriculture; means of transport and communication; the banks; the property of state-run trade organisations and public utilities, and other state-run undertakings; most urban housing; and other property necessary for state purposes. || Article 12. The property of collective farms and other co-operative organisations, and of their joint undertakings, comprises the means of production and other assets which they require for the purposes laid down in their rules. The land held by collective farms is secured to them for their free use in perpetuity. The state promotes development of collective farm-and-co-operative property and its approximation to state property. Collective farms, like other land users, are obliged to make effective and thrifty use of the land and to increase its fertility. || Article 13 (extract). Earned income forms the basis of the personal property of Soviet citizens. [...] Citizens may be granted the use of plots of land, in the manner prescribed by law, for a subsidiary small-holding (including the keeping of livestock and poultry), for fruit and vegetable growing or for building an individual dwelling.

ownership.defaultNote: state property by law (1977 Constitution, art. 11)

regimes.industriesJudged: Jev (jev-1.14.0), two Scores per industry; model judgments, not measurement
regimes.notes: Agriculture was not all state property: collective farms were cooperative property (art. 12) and collective farmers were 11.0% of employment in 1980 (Narodnoe khozyaistvo 1980, p. 356); private plots gave about one-fourth of farm output on 3.5% of the cropland (CIA 1981, ER 81-10309). The drawing keeps every summit the state's by law. Spending and revenue are shares of a GDP the CASE paper prints (619 billion rubles) without naming its source.
